/WEDNESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Issued at 302 AM MST Sun Nov 15 2026

A little more uncertainty exists than usual four days out for a 
typical long-term forecast period. Recent GFS and European runs just 
continue to struggle on agreement regarding to the specifics of 
Wednesday's system. Guidance does still agree on a weak longwave 
troughing across the Northern Plains post-deamplification over the 
Western CONUS. Also, a jet streak aloft containing southwesterly 
upper-level flow is still anticipated to dominate our area. Where 
these models diverge is actually the position of said trough 
relative to the county warning area (CWA). The GFS and associated 
ensemble has the trough digging a bit more southward than the Euro 
and Canadian runs. This will become relevant as it may mean the 
surface low tracks further south than expected, boosting 
precipitation chances for Wednesday. Anyways, the low is still 
anticipated to track off to the northeast and bring a cold front 
through the region. Despite this recent development, guidance has 
actually held steady with probability of precipitation (PoPs) 
remaining around 5-15%. Dry air entrainment, via surface winds from 
the southwest, should limit development of precipitation; Therefore, 
confidence is low (20%) on any rainfall occurring.

Looking ahead to Thursday, a ridge is now likely to influence our 
coverage area briefly then move off to the northeast. Southwest flow 
should continue aloft and high pressure/subsidence should allow 
surface temperatures to recover from Wednesday's cold front. Late 
next week, things start to get interesting again as another trough 
slides through the Rockies and across our CWA. This negatively 
tilted Rossby wave should bring with it another jet streak as well 
as another surface low-pressure system/cold front combo. Interestingly
enough, the low is likely to take a similar path to Wednesday's
system, propagating off to the northeast with the cold front 
moving eastward across Kansas and into the lower- Missouri 
Valley. Said low is actually forecasted to form over Northern 
Colorado which would influence our area better than Wednesday's 
system. Thus, guidance follows suit with rainfall chances a bit 
higher on Friday. PoPs in the 30-50% presents with the main 
precip clearing out by afternoon Saturday. Light to moderate 
rain showers are all that should come from this system with QPFs
forecasted in the 0.01 to 0.05 range. That being said, up to 
300 j/kg of SB CAPE is possible so convection (a few 
thunderstorms) cannot be ruled out and this would boost 
accumulations a bit for some localized areas.

Temperatures mid-late next week should be quite pleasant for this 
time of the year. Average to above average highs are forecasted 
through Saturday with Friday being the warmest of the four days in 
this long-term period. Highs in the 60s across the entire CWA is to 
be expected Wednesday. Thursday should see a slight cooldown after 
the first cold front moves through but 50s/low 60s are still likely. 
Friday should bounce back nicely with more consistent 60s and a few 
areas may even reach the low 70s. After the second cold front moves 
through late Friday, highs are anticipated to fall back into the 
50s. 

Breezy conditions should continue through the middle of next 
week via the first upper-level jet. Surface winds 10-25 mph gusting 
up to 40 mph are likely. Winds decrease slight Thursday then pick 
back up on Friday with the second jet. Finally, Saturday's winds 
should also die down a little to 10-20 mph with gusts up to 25-30 
mph (35 mph in localized areas of eastern Colorado). Fire weather is 
likely to remain a non-concern through next weekend. Wednesday 
will likely be the driest day with relative humidities dropping 
as low as 25-30% but areas where it'll be the driest shouldn't 
have strong/gusty winds occurring at the same time.
